title: Author Robert Paarlberg argues against buying organic
summary: Book excerpt arguing organic food is overpriced, no safer or more nutritious, land-hungry and dominated by industrial farms, with livestock welfare as its one clear plus.

assertions.quote: the average retail price (by volume) for organic produce was 54 percent higher than for conventional produce
It also requires more land for every bushel of production
there is little or no scientific evidence to support these claims
since the 1970s increased regulation plus reduced spraying have brought risks under control
Copper sulfate is permitted as a fungicide because it isn’t synthetic
animal products cannot be labeled organic if the animals were fed or treated with antibiotics
Producers of organic meat, milk, and eggs are required to provide their animals with more space to move around
Most organic food on the market today comes from highly specialized, industrial-scale farms
This is not a science-based distinction.
without nitrogen fertilizer, 40 percent of the increase in food production needed to feed these much larger numbers would never have taken place
